title: Germ descent for cartesian higher images
statement: Let k be a field, D:I→Over(Spec k) a small cofiltered diagram of qcqs schemes over k with affine transition maps, c a cone whose underlying scheme cone is limiting with qcqs structure map, f:X→Spec k qcqs, F an arbitrary abelian étale sheaf on X, and q≥0. Fix a geometric point at s of c.pt.left. For every geometric point of the limiting base, every element of the cartesian limit higher-image fiber is the image of an element of one stage fiber along its canonical leg. Here stages, legs and transitions are the canonical constructions in the cited statement dependencies. No hypothesis of invertible stage exchange is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 59.51.8, second proof; support statement isolated by S4

proof.text: Apply exists_abelianDerivedHomology_sections_comparison to the limit derived image. Local surjectivity induces surjectivity on the geometric fiber, so lift y to a raw germ and represent it on an etale U. The dense affine etale inclusion and the point covering condition give an affine refinement W with the same germ.

Apply exists_cartesianHigherImage_raw_affine_factorization to the raw class on W. Obtain a stage i and a raw derived morphism t whose composite with the shifted cartesian leg is the refined raw class. Map t to a section of the stage homology sheaf with the same derived-Hom-to-homology comparison.

Naturality of the homology shift isomorphism and preservation of composition identify the image of that stage section with the limit comparison section. Apply the fiber map naturality equation and the affine-refinement cone equation to identify its germ with y. No invertibility of stage exchange is assumed.

proof_origin.place: Second proof, affine etale descent and continuity
